design.site_summary: A partially shaded balcony with moderate moisture and safe conditions for a curious dog named Max.
design.layout_strategy: Trailing edible herbs on the railing at eye level, upright aromatic shrubs at mid height against the wall, and a low grazing zone of safe herbs along the balcony floor edge for Max.
design.combination_logic: This combination blends fine-textured herbs with sturdy shrubs, creating a dynamic contrast in height and aroma that changes from lush spring growth to woody textures in winter.

zones.placement: on the east-facing railing, 3 hours of morning sun, sheltered from afternoon heat.

plants.why: Provides vertical height and a pleasant citrus scent at eye level.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as the tall structural element with delicate leaves.

maintenance: Water twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn.
Prune back lightly in early spring to encourage bushy growth.

zones.placement: on the floor edge, bright morning light and easily reachable by Max.

plants.why: Provides a soft, low ground cover that is safe and engaging for Max.
plants.role_in_combination: Contributes a dense carpet of delicate green foliage and textural contrast.

maintenance: Water weekly when soil feels dry to the touch.
Trim back after flowering to keep the mat dense and tidy.

care_instructions.task: Water all containers thoroughly until drainage occurs
care_instructions.frequency: Twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture levels using finger test

care_cautions: Overwatering the railing edible zone can lead to root rot in the Lemon Verbena container.
The ground grazing zone with Chamomile must be monitored to ensure Max does not dig up the roots.
design.pet_safety_note: This design keeps Max safe by exclusively featuring verified safe plants and placing the grazing zone within his reach for safe exploration.
